$comment: Ontology for the AS-Level Physics (CAIE 9702) knowledge graph — the single source of truth for (a) the LLM extractor's allowed_nodes / allowed_relationships constraint and (b) output validation. Direction convention matches backend/tool/knowledge_graph.py: source PREREQUISITE_OF target means 'source is a prerequisite of target' (target depends on source). Three layers: concrete (Topic/Concept/Formula/Skill) + abstract (BigIdea). BigIdea nodes are teacher-curated (never LLM-extracted); Concept->BigIdea assignment (EXEMPLIFIES) is a classification task.
subject: AS-Level Physics (CAIE 9702)

entity_types.definition: A syllabus topic or chapter heading. Forms the fixed skeleton of the graph, seeded by RULE from the syllabus (NOT LLM-extracted).
A physical concept, quantity, or phenomenon a student must understand: scalar/vector quantities, conserved quantities, forces, wave phenomena, electrical quantities, etc.
A formula, equation, or law expressing a quantitative relationship between concepts. Put the symbolic form in the 'expression' field.
A transferable procedural skill or technique needed to solve problems, independent of any single topic.

An abstract, cross-topic organizing principle that unifies many concrete concepts and gives students the 'framework'. This layer turns a knowledge graph into a knowledge framework. CURATED by the teacher, NOT extracted by LLM — fixed small set to avoid abstraction drift.
examples: Waves transfer energy without net matter transfer

relation_types.definition: source is a prerequisite of target: target cannot be properly learned until source is mastered. Directed: source -> target.
source (a topic/concept/formula) requires the procedural skill target in order to be applied. Directed: source -> target.
examples: Free-Body Diagrams -> resolve a vector into components

relation_types.definition: source (a Concept/Formula/Skill) belongs to target (a Topic). Attaches extracted entities to the syllabus skeleton. Directed: source -> target.

source (a Concept/Formula/Skill) exemplifies target (a BigIdea). How the concrete layer hangs under the abstract framework layer; enables knowledge_framework to 'walk up' from a weak concept to its unifying big idea. Assignment is a CLASSIFICATION over a closed label set (LLM does this reliably), NOT open extraction. Directed: source -> target.
Students frequently confuse source and target in actual answers (an ERROR pattern). Source of truth is error/错题 data, NOT the notes. Symmetric.

source and target form a conceptual opposition pair that the curriculum deliberately juxtaposes; understanding the distinction IS the learning objective. Source of truth is the notes/curriculum (unlike COMMONLY_CONFUSED, which is error-driven). A-Level physics leans heavily on these pairs, so mapping them is core to forming the framework. Symmetric.
source and target frequently appear together in the same exam question or as consecutive steps of a solution. Symmetric.
The same class of problem can be solved using source OR target as alternative methods/starting points. The key 'which-tool' decision edge. Symmetric in practice; store one direction.
examples: suvat method <-> energy method (motion under gravity)
